notes: Hermes ships a NATIVE autonomous self-prompting loop: /goal <text> registers a standing goal, immediately enqueues the goal text as the first user message, and after every turn a judge call decides done/continue — on continue the '[Continuing toward your standing goal]' prompt is fed back into the SAME session as an ordinary user message (hermes_cli/goals.py, cli.py:_maybe_continue_goal_after_turn). Each iteration is therefore a complete turn that ends with finish_reason='stop' BEFORE the judge is consulted, so the store legitimately reports turn-over between iterations and the daemon cycles ready/working per iteration rather than holding one continuous working span — the same relaxation the claudecode sibling documented for its Stop-hook /goal. What this spec asserts instead is the thing that actually proves autonomy: iter2_start must reach working with NO driver-sent message between iter1_done and it. hermes is a PRESESSION adapter here — ProcessOwnedStore whose sessions row is INSERTed only on the first user message, so a transient proc-<PID> row is born first and the real store session (a different id) is born ready afterwards; every post-birth phase anchors to the real session. observations: tokens verified nonzero on live sessions rows (input_tokens ~16k); cost_nonzero=false is provisional (hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 subscription-included and irrlicht re-prices from its alias table, which has no gpt-5.6-luna entry); model left UNPINNED for record to fill because the recording home's config.yaml is not knowable from here.

text: Process scanner mints the transient proc-<PID> pre-session in ready — hermes' sessions row does not exist until the first user message, so this is the first thing the daemon can see
The real store session (a DIFFERENT id, source='cli') is born ready once /goal writes the first user message — the REPL boot is slow (~35 tools + ~68 skills), hence the wide budget
Spec: 'ready -> working at loop start' — /goal <condition> enqueues the goal text as a user message and drives iteration 1
Iteration 1 completes: the assistant row carries finish_reason='stop', so the turn is genuinely over and the session settles to ready while the goal judge runs
THE autonomy assertion: the session returns to working on the SAME session with no user and no driver input in between — the judge said 'continue' and hermes fed its own continuation prompt back in
Iteration 2 completes back to ready — at least two self-driven turns, satisfying the scenario's '>= 2 turns'

Spec: 'after the goal is reached: working -> ready' — the loop terminates (judge verdict done, or /goal clear) and final state is ready. The loop may run a third iteration before converging, so the only strict invariant here is that the session never enters waiting across the tail of the run; the matcher may satisfy this at iter2_done itself (delta 0), exactly as the claudecode sibling does, because the convergence turn's timing is non-deterministic
